In ancient Egypt, the horizon was believed to be where the dead entered the afterlife. The Great Sphinx could be guarding that sacred spot.

And who built the Great Sphinx? While the nearby pyramids have inscriptions and clues about their builders, the Great Sphinx reveals almost no clues. Scientists think it was created by the same team that constructed one of the pyramids. But since these pyramids were built at different times, it's hard to know for sure which team that was. And here's another mystery about the Sphinx's construction—it was never finished. Scholars don't know why, but the builders seem to have abandoned the project shortly before its completion.

I was surprised to learn this, but sand has buried the Great Sphinx on and off throughout most of its existence. According to a story from around 1400 BC, a prince was hunting in the hot desert and saw the Sphinx's head sticking out of the sand. He decided to sit in the shade under the head. The prince fell asleep, and when the sun reached its highest point, the statue appeared to the prince in a dream. It said that if the prince uncovered the rest of the statue, the prince would become the next pharaoh. The prince did as the statue said, and he became King Thutmose IV! Oh, and over time the Great Sphinx was buried under sand again, of course!

Being buried under the sand may have helped to protect the Sphinx. If the Sphinx had not been buried for most of its existence, it would have disappeared long ago. Still, the statue has suffered a lot of damage over time. Its nose is missing—gone forever, probably chiseled out by looters. But that's not the worst problem. The statue is slowly turning to dust! Limestone is soft, and wind, water, and sand have weakened the statue over time.

Two more recent threats to the Great Sphinx are pollution and rising groundwater. Today the stone is treated with special chemicals that help protect it from the pollution. And holes have been drilled in several spots near the statue to prevent water damage. Luckily, scientists also used sophisticated laser scanning equipment to closely examine the statue. The equipment helped to identify its weak spots, and now scientists can take steps to limit future damage.

Thousands of years ago, as the Great Sphinx sat here, gazing at the rising sun, it was probably guarding the pharaohs' entryway to the afterlife. Now it's our time to be the guards. We have to watch the ancient Sphinx carefully and take good care of it. That way, thousands of years from now, people will still be admiring its beauty.

Bulgaria is a country nestled in the southeastern corner of Europe. Not much is heard about it on the news, and it is still largely undiscovered by tourists. It lies north of Greece and south of the Danube River. To its east is the Black Sea, and its neighbor to the west is Serbia.

Bulgaria is one of the oldest settled lands in all of Europe. It has a rich history and diverse customs, and its people are proud of their heritage. The Bulgarians have a rich tradition of celebrating festivals and gatherings.

In the past Bulgaria was largely an agricultural nation because of its fertile soil. It produced an abundance of vegetables, fruits, grain, and products from farm animals. Today the country is industrialized, and many products are imported. Local farms, however, continue to grow a variety of harvests.

The Bulgarian people continue to grow one item that has perfume companies from Paris to New York talking. It is very hard to produce, and it is very expensive. It is the pure rose oil extracted from a small pink rose named Rosa damascene , and it is an important ingredient in many perfumes.

In the center of Bulgaria lies the Valley of the Roses. It is a fertile valley covered in tiny pink roses whose sweet aroma can be felt like a perfume in the air. The valley’s moderate climate allows the roses to grow in perfect conditions. The local people have been cultivating these unique flowers for hundreds of years.

The farmers who live in the valley pick the roses when they start to bloom in the beginning of June. They gather the tiny buds very early in the morning, just before sunrise, because that is when the roses are still fresh and full of dew.

Traditionally, it was the young girls and women who harvested the roses and collected them in their baskets. They would put the very first flower they picked in their hair for decoration. While they worked, they sang the traditional songs sung every year during the rose harvest. Today the production is much faster, but the roses are still picked by hand by local farmers.

After the roses are picked, they are rushed to the rose distillery before the sun has a chance to dry them. Their petals are collected in large pots and pressed to extract tiny amounts of oil. It takes almost two tons of petals to produce just one pound of pure rose oil.

The rose oil is very aromatic and very expensive. It is even more expensive than gold. Besides its use in perfumes, rose oil is used in medicines, cosmetics, soaps, and even in rose petal jam! Today picking the prized blossoms is the main industry in the Rose Valley, and this industry continues to grow.

Every year the first day of picking is celebrated with an annual Rose Festival. This daylong festival is usually held in the first week of June. The pickers wear their traditional costumes decorated with garlands of roses. They hold a beauty contest and choose a Rose Queen. Later when the harvest is over, the Rose Queen rewards the most skilled picker with a crown.

The title of Rose Queen is an important honor for the lucky girl who receives it, and the festival itself has become a celebration of beauty. Since roses are a symbol of beauty and because the flowers are used in the beauty industry, the festival organizers felt that they needed to nominate a beauty queen. That’s how the Rose Queen was born.

Many Bulgarian actors, musicians, and circus performers flock to the Rose Valley every year to perform in the festival. It has even become an international destination for tourists from all over the world. The Rose Festival ends with a carnival where local people dress up in costumes and dance all night long.

The very first Rose Festival was held in 1903 in the nearby town of Kazanlak. It slowly grew from a small gathering of rose pickers to a national event with many towns and villages participating. It keeps the traditions associated with the rose harvest alive, and it makes the local farmers very proud of their labor.

Bulgarians are very proud of their rose oil production, which carries the name of their country far and beyond. They feel that the rose is the queen of all flowers, and that is why they have picked it to be their national flower.

Today the Rose Festival and the harvest go hand in hand. Local people gather to celebrate the beautiful tradition of rose picking, and international companies continue to import the best rose oil in the world from the Valley of the Roses.

Bonjour ! My name is Sophie, and I live in France. Today I am visiting my grandfather at his vineyard where he grows grapes for making wine. Wine is made from grapes and contains alcohol. I can’t drink wine because I’m too young. I can tell you how it is made because my grandfather makes wine!

Today adults drink wine with dinner at home or in a restaurant, but wine has a long history. Archaeologists discovered wine jugs in Iran that were seven thousand years old. In Ancient Egypt the pharaohs were buried with wine so they could drink wine in the afterlife.
The ancient Greeks and Romans drank wine mixed with water and used wine in religious ceremonies. When the Roman Empire expanded, the Romans brought wine grapes to France, Italy, Spain, and Germany.

From the fifth century until the Middle Ages, Christian monks were the main winemakers of Europe. The monks made wine at the monasteries where they lived. They improved the quality of wine and developed better methods for making wine.
Making wine is not difficult, but you need lots of patience. It takes at least a year before the wine is ready! Let me tell you how my grandfather makes wine.

First Grandfather grows the grapes in cool weather with lots of sun. In France where we live, the weather is perfect for growing grapes. Grapes grow on vines, and the field where the grapes grow is called a vineyard.

When the grapes are ripe, Grandfather harvests the grapes from the vines. He takes them to the winery and puts them in a huge vat. The ripe grapes are juicy and sweet and full of sugar. The next step is to crush the grapes.

A long time ago, people used their feet to crush the grapes. They would climb into the vat with bare feet and jump and stomp until the grapes were crushed. Boy, that sounds like fun, and very messy too! My grandfather uses a machine to crush the grapes.

Crushing the grapes breaks the skins and turns them into a wet, juicy pulp. Over the next few days, yeast on the grape skins causes the wine to ferment. When the wine ferments, the sugar in the grapes changes to alcohol. The juice and pulp in the vat will begin to fizz.

After a week the fizzing subsides. Now my grandfather must separate the liquid from the skins, pulp, and seeds. He uses a machine called a winepress, and then he pours the wine into barrels. Until now, the wine has been open to the air. But now the barrels are sealed to keep the air away from the wine.

Three weeks later the fermentation is finally complete. Now the wine is ready for the final step. This step is called racking. My grandfather filters the leftover yeast, grape seeds, and grape skins from the wine, and scrapes the barrel clean. Then he pours the wine back into the barrel and seals it airtight.

The barrels of wine are stored in a cool, dark place. Four months later, Grandfather racks the wine one more time. Now the wine is perfectly clear. Grandfather puts the barrels away in a cool, dark place again and leaves them for a whole year! My grandfather keeps his barrels of wine in the cellar.
One year later, the wine is ready! Sometimes vineyards wait two years or longer before they sell their wine, and some wines are kept for decades. People say that wine gets better with age.

The wine is poured into bottles, and each bottle is plugged with a cork to prevent air getting in. Corks are made from the bark of the cork tree, which grows mainly in Portugal. Cork is very elastic, but it is also airtight. It is ideal for wine bottles.

France is famous for its wine, and many tourists visit France just to tour the wineries. However, wine grapes are grown in warm climates all over the world. France and Italy have the oldest wineries, but Australia, New Zealand, Chile, South Africa, and California are all famous for their wine as well.

Now I will help Grandfather get the wine ready for the stores. First, we put fancy labels on the bottles. Then, we put the wine bottles into boxes. Tomorrow a truck will pick up the boxes and take them to restaurants, bars, supermarkets, and wine stores.
Thank you for visiting my grandfather’s vineyard. Now you know everything about making wine. Next time you can help us harvest the grapes!

New York, Paris, Tokyo, Moscow, Seoul, Beijing, Delhiㅡmore than 150 cities around the world have subways. A subway is an electric underground railway. It makes it easy to get around downtown and connects a city to the suburbs. The oldest subway, and one of the biggest, is the London Tube.

The London subway is called the Tube because its tunnels are narrow and round like a tube. In fact, its tunnels are the smallest in the world, but the Tube is one of the longest subways, with 391 kilometers of track.

The Tube was the world’s first underground rail system. It was built in 1863. But why did the city of London decide to build a railway underground? Well, in those days, the streets of London were very busy and dirty!

Back then, the cheapest way to get around town was the omnibusㅡa horse-drawn bus. Twenty people could sit inside an omnibus, but it wasn’t a pleasant experience. It was crowded, and there was dirty straw on the floor.
People complained a lot about riding in an omnibus. So in 1836 the London Times newspaper published suggestions to make the journey more pleasant.
They included:
1. Sit up straight and don’t take the space of two people.
2. Do not sit on the straw. You are not in a pigsty.
3. If you have a dog, make sure it is small and has a leash.
4. Do not bring large parcelsㅡan omnibus is not a van.
5. Don’t expect the omnibus conductor to have change; he is not a banker.
6. Don’t act like you are better than other passengers. If you can afford to
ride a private horse and carriage, then do so!

Riding inside the omnibus may have been bad, but stepping out of the bus and onto the London streets was even worse. With thousands of horses trotting along, the streets were filled withㅡyou guessed itㅡhorse poo!

The horse dung was so bad that people, often children, worked as crossing sweepers. Their job was to sweep in front of rich people as they crossed the road. You can imagine that if people could avoid traveling in the streets, they would!

So when the Tube started in the late 1800s, it was a great success! Back then, the first Tube carriages were long, narrow, and had no windows. The Tube’s original designers thought there was nothing to see in a tunnel, so why have windows?

By the twentieth century, the Tube had expanded all over London. During World War I and World War II, Londoners used the Tube stations as bomb shelters. London was one of the worst-bombed cities during World War II. People would buy tickets and never come out, because the Tube station was the safest place to be. From 1939 to 1945, nearly 63 million people stayed in 79 of London’s Tube stations. Restaurants and libraries were set up underground, and performers entertained people.

Even with modern technology, the Tube still has problems. There’s always the danger of flooding from the Thames River. After giant flood gates were built in 1984, flooding greatly decreased, but some Tube stations still get flooded during thunderstorms.

In the summers it is very hot inside a Tube carriage, and air conditioners can’t be installed for two reasons. First, they give off too much heat, and second, the carriages are too small. The mayor of London offered a reward of ten thousand pounds for a solution to this problem!

If you ever go to London, make sure you take the Tube! Look for a round red sign and go down the stairs. Buy a ticket, wait on the narrow platform, then get on the Tubeㅡand remember you’re sitting inside a part of London’s history!

Josh and Anne are gearing up for another adventure in the great outdoors. For this trip, they will spend two weeks backpacking through New Zealand, which sounds like fun, don't you think? However, this adventure will require getting some special gear before they head out.

Anne and Josh decide to visit a store that sells a lot of backpacking supplies. Anne knows that the most important piece of equipment for when she's about to do a lot of hiking, is strong boots. She tries out a number of boots, walking up and down plastic mountains in the store to test how well they hold the ground. It looks like she has found some boots that are very light, waterproof, strong, and her favorite color─yellow!
Josh, meanwhile, knows that the next most important purchase is poles. Scientists have recently discovered that walking downhill with a lot of weight is difficult for the knees to handle.

In fact, a lot of people injure their knees by slipping downhill, but poles help the knees by providing extra support and balance. So Josh chooses some poles that are lightweight but strong enough to support his weight and grip the ground.

The last big purchase is a backpack. Backpacks come in all colors, sizes, and weights. Bags that hold over seven kilograms have a padded strap that goes around the waist to help lift the weight off the shoulders. Josh picks a brown pack that will help him hide in the trees, and Anne picks a pack with her favorite color─yellow!

There are a lot more pieces of equipment that Josh and Anne will need to go on their trip, such as headlamps, sleeping bags, a cookstove, food, hiking clothes, a first aid kit, and bug repellant. However, all of this can get expensive, so they borrow a lot of these things from their friends. "In order to stay safe when you go backpacking, it's important to have good gear," Josh says.

Their bags are packed, and they are on their way to New Zealand! New Zealand is a beautiful country with many kinds of landscapes. There are beaches, forests, jungles, plains, mountains, and volcanoes, just to name a few.

The country is about the same size as Korea, just a tiny bit bigger. But there are seventy million people living in Korea and only four million living in New Zealand. Of course, you can change the total to four million and two, now that Josh and Anne have landed!

There are countless trails and hikes to choose from when you visit this beautiful country. Josh and Anne decide to try the most famous trail in New Zealand, which is nicknamed the Most Beautiful Walk in the World. It is a trail called the Milford Track. It will take four days to hike the 53 kilometers from one side of the mountain to the other. And because so many people like to visit Milford, they will sleep in huts instead of tents because it is easier on the wildlife.

Josh and Anne arrive at Milford on a very sunny day. After walking a few kilometers, they pass by a river that is a color of blue Anne has never seen in a river before. She is tempted to dive in, but it is too cold!

Later on in the hike, Josh meets a kea. Don't be fooled, this is a very smart and talented bird. While people aren't looking, it will unzip their backpacks and steal their lunches. Josh gets close enough to take a picture and leaves the disappointed kea waiting for its next victim.

At the top of the mountain is Mackinnon Pass. The view is breathtaking, and so is the freezing wind! As they walk down the other side of the mountain, Josh and Anne are glad they have their poles. Along the way they find a powerful waterfall.

Anne decides to test how waterproof her jacket is and steps underneath the falls. "It felt like a massage!" she says, emerging from the waterfall dry and smiling. The four days of hiking go by faster than they expected, and soon Josh and Anne are at the end of the trail.
"What did you think of Milford?" Anne asked.
"It's so beautiful, my feet aren't even tired!" said Josh.
"I agree. I can't wait to come back and do it again!" said Anne.
The first trail was a success. With another 12 days to go, Josh and Anne are thankful they have such great gear and such a beautiful country to visit.
"Is your air on?" asks Josh.
"Is your air on?" asks Anne. "Okay, let's go!"

Today Josh and Anne are taking us on a scuba-diving adventure near the Similan Islands in Thailand. The water here is so clear that we can see things thirty meters away, and that's pretty far for being underwater! Whenever people go scuba diving, they swim in a group for safety, so we had better stay together!

There are hundreds of great places to scuba dive in the world, and each of them is different. Some places are very cold, or are filled with seaweed, or have only very small animals. The Similan Islands, however, are great because the water is 28 degrees Celsius and crystal clear, and there are lots of big fish.

In fact, look over there! Josh has found a moray eel hiding in the rocks. Don't worry; it is more frightened of us than we are of it. Look at its sharp teeth! It has two sets of jaws to pull its prey in, so keep your hands far away! Eels aren't very friendly creatures, as you can tell, and they mostly live alone. So we probably won't see another eel for quite a while.

Did you know that there are hundreds of plants that live underwater? Thailand has many kinds. One plantlike creature is called coral, and there are two kinds: hard coral and soft coral. A coral is built from live cells that stack on top of each other in layers. When the outer layer gets old, a new layer of cells forms around it so the plant grows taller or wider.

Like their names suggest, hard coral is stiff, while soft coral is able to sway with the ocean current. Both soft and hard coral grow very slowly. Look, this fan coral grows about one centimeter each year, so Anne is careful not to touch it as she swims by. Touching a coral can kill it, and sometimes it can hurt us too so we stay far away.

Look, down at the bottom—there's a whale shark, the biggest fish in the world! Anne is trying to get her picture taken with it, but don't worry, this shark won't bite. Whale sharks only eat small animals and tiny plants that float in the water called plankton. Still, we're careful not to disturb the shark since this is its home.

Josh is checking his pressure gauges, and signals to Anne that he is almost out of air. Men use up air faster than women because their lungs are bigger and because they have more muscle, but I think we have enough time to look at just a couple more creatures.

Oh no, Anne is giving the danger signal! She found a sea snake. This underwater creature may be tiny, but its venom is twenty times more poisonous than any snake on land! It eats mostly small fish by paralyzing them first with one quick bite. It takes less than a second for its venom to work. The sea snake seems to be a little hungry, so we'll move on.

Here is Josh's favorite animal, the cuttlefish. Many people eat cuttlefish thinking it is an ordinary squid, but it is really an amazing animal. Watch carefully. The mother cuttlefish is trying to protect its baby by distracting us. See how its skin is changing colors so that we can see it better?

Cuttlefish can change the color and texture of their skin to match anything around them. For example, if there is a field of black rocks nearby, their skin will turn bumpy and black. If they swim by green seaweed, they will turn smooth and green. If you put down a purple polka-dot blanket, their skin will have polka dots!
It looks like Josh is low on air. It's time to return to our own world above-water, but don't be disappointed. There will always be another adventure!

25.title: Chinese Opera: Singing with a Squeaky Voice

paragraphs.text: What art form is nine hundred years old and includes acrobatics, martial arts, and squeaky singing? If you guessed the Chinese opera, you’re right! If you’re wondering what the Chinese opera is like, and why the singers have squeaky voices, keep reading!

If you were to attend the Chinese opera, this is what it would be like. First you would see an empty stage. The actors want people in the audience to use their imagination, so they use only a few stage decorations. The performers also need a lot of room on stage for their acrobatics and martial arts.

Next you might see a mini orchestra. The orchestra is usually made up of string instruments like guitars, wind instruments like flutes, drums, and wooden clappers. These are used to make music as well as sound effects, like a horse galloping or a rooster crowing.

Then you will see the actors come on stage. There are four groups of characters: Sheng, Dan, Jing, and Chou. Sheng are the men in the opera, such as an uncle or a little boy. Unlike the actors in the other three groups, they don’t paint their faces.

Dan are the women in the play, and they are the ones who sing with the squeaky voices. Jing are the warriors or demons. And Chou are the clowns. They wear white makeup on their noses and their job is to keep the audience laughing.

So why do the Dan sing with squeaky voices? Even though the Dan are women, the actors playing them are almost always men. When a man pretends to have a woman’s voice, it often sounds squeaky. Nine hundred years ago, the Chinese opera was performed outside, so the actors had to sing loudly. Their voices weren’t supposed to sound pretty, just loud.

It takes a lifetime of studying to be an actor in the Chinese opera. Historically, children were sold to the opera to begin training when they were young. Parents knew that the opera would give their children a good life.

Even though the children were young, they would get up early every morning to begin their exercises, and they would practice all day long. One actor remembers having to do handstands on a chair for hours and practicing five thousand kicks and punches in one day. The children were forced to work very hard, but it made their bodies some of the strongest in China.

One of the most famous stars of the Chinese opera is Jackie Chan. When he was six, his parents signed a ten-year contract so he could be trained in the opera. When Jackie Chan became an adult, the Chinese opera was not very popular anymore. So, Jackie Chan used what he had learned at the opera to become one of the best martial arts superstars in movie history.
The Chinese opera is a lot more than beautiful costumes, amazing acrobatics, martial arts stunts, and stories. It is an art form that brings together the best cultural traditions of China.

I go to school in the world’s biggest classroom. My classroom is more than double the size of the United Kingdom, more than one and a half million square kilometers. I only see my teacher and classmates a few times a year! I am a student at the School of the Air.

The School of the Air is in Australia, and it teaches around one thousand students nationwide. Many students, like me, live in isolated places in the vast area of Australia known as the outback. The outback is the huge desert-like area in the middle of Australia, away from its coasts. Very few people live here. My nearest classmate is a four-hour drive away, and the nearest town is a six-hour drive.

I live at Pine Creek Cattle Station, Northern Territory, Australia. Outback kids are different from city kids—I am 12 years old, but I ride a horse, work on a farm, and drive a motorcycle. I don’t have a license though!
When I am 13, I will leave home and go to a boarding school in Darwin. Until then I will study at the School of the Air. How do I study? The word "air" is a clue—the School of the Air uses the radio.

Monday to Friday I turn on the radio at eight o’clock. First up is the assembly. During assembly we sing the national anthem and the school song. Then we listen to other students do something special, like play the flute, read a poem they’ve written, or tell some jokes.

After the assembly there is lesson time for two hours. Mom or Dad sits next to me during lessons and helps me with my homework. After lunch there are extra activities. I am in the choir. At first it's strange singing into a radio microphone by yourself, but you get used to it!
On Wednesday I learn the flute over the radio, but Friday is my favorite day. After class is finished, I have a Girl Guides meeting—also on the radio! We are the Guides of the Air.

But how do I study over the radio? First, I use a two-way radio, which means I can talk and listen to my teacher and the other students. Second, I use the Internet to email my teacher and look at websites for information and research.

Third, every two weeks my teacher sends me books and homework through the mail. Fourth, I attend a school camp a few times a year, where I meet my teacher and my classmates face-to-face! Finally, my teacher comes and stays at my house for one week a year.

Fifty years ago the School of the Air was very different. In those days the Flying Doctor was the only radio contact for people living in isolation. The Flying Doctor service is made up of doctors and nurses who fly to people in remote areas who need medical care. They give people medicine and medical advice or take them to the hospital.

The Flying Doctor’s radio, however, wasn’t used just for medical news or advice. It also broadcast local news with its weekly galah session. A galah is an Australian bird that chatters a lot, and during the galah sessions, people talked to each other on the radio.

Adelaide Miethke was a teacher in Alice Springs. She listened to the galah sessions on the radio and recognized that outback kids were very shy because they didn’t get to meet other children very often.

Adelaide Miethke suggested to the government that they start the School of the Air. The first broadcast was from Alice Springs in 1951, using the Flying Doctor’s radio. Now there are more than 16 Schools of the Air around Australia.
Mom said that back then, the radio didn’t sound so clear. There were often breaks and strange noises. The teacher even had to power the radio with her feet!

Of course things have changed. The Internet and satellites mean that radio lessons may disappear altogether. In the future I will probably use an electronic whiteboard and receive my lessons via satellite. In the meantime I enjoy my lessons over the airwaves.
Over and out!

Is your helmet on tight? Is your harness buckled? Are you feeling courageous? Well then, let's fly! Today Josh and Anne are taking us on an adventure through the skies. With no motor, no parachute, and no hot air balloon, they are going flying. How? With hang gliders!
Josh and Anne are joining us today in Queenstown, New Zealand, a city whose people are known for having fun in the great outdoors.
"I have always wanted to fly, and I think hang gliding sounds like fun. Do you want to come?" says Josh.
"It sounds exciting, but I'm a little nervous about it. Then again, it's good to try new things . . . so let's go!" says Anne.

Hang gliding is actually very easy. Josh will fly with a championship glider named Tom. Tom is great at doing stunts and flying fast. Anne will fly with a glide instructor named Rick, who is good at teaching beginners.

With the hang gliders packed on the roof of the van, everyone drives to the top of the mountain that overlooks Queenstown. It takes the instructors only twenty minutes to assemble poles and pieces into a complete glider. Josh and Anne seem pretty impressed.
Rick calls Anne over for her first lesson on flying. "Okay, first, you need a helmet that fits your head well. How does this one work?"
"It feels comfortable and nice and hard," says Anne.

Then Rick explains the next piece of equipment. "Great. Next you need a harness. This one should fit you. It looks like a sleeping bag, but it is very strong. It will hook you to the glider tightly so you can't fall out."
"I'd better not fall out!"

While Rick and Anne get her harness fitted, Tom gets Josh ready for their jump. "Cheers, Josh. When we're hooked up to the glider, I'll ask if you're ready. If you feel nervous and you're not ready, say ‘Wait.' But, if you feel ready, say ‘Ready.' Got it?"
"Excellent! I'm ready to fly already! Let's go!" says Josh.

"In just a minute, we'll start back here, away from the edge. When you say ready, I'll count one, two, three. At one, we start running. At two, we run harder. At three, we throw ourselves off the cliff."
"I throw myself off the cliff?" Josh is worried.

"Don't worry," explains Tom. "Your wings will be attached. It's important that you run faster and faster as I count from one to three. When we run fast off the edge, it gives our glider momentum and pushes us out. But if we go slowly, we'll fall straight down. Got it?"
"I got it. No worries."

Running in a harness is more difficult than it looks. It's like running with a sleeping bag around your legs. While Josh practices running, Rick teaches Anne how to steer. "Turning the glider is really simple, Anne. There is a triangular bar in front that is attached to the top of the glider. If we want to go left, we push the bar to the right. If we want to go up, we push the bar forward. And pulling the bar towards us sends us down. But I don't recommend that."
"I think I'll let you do the steering, thanks," says Anne.
Once everyone has practiced, it's time to get strapped into the gliders. Anne reminds herself it's good to try new things, and Josh reminds himself of the one-two-three. Josh and Tom go first.
"Ready?"
"Ready!"
"One . . . two . . . three . . ."

And they're off! Anne and Rick are up next, and soon they are flying right above Josh and Tom. While Josh and Tom are diving and flying sideways, Anne and Rick take in the view. Hang gliding is a nature-friendly sport because there is no noise and no pollution.
Both gliders circle the fields below. And it's a perfect landing! "That was the most beautiful flight I could have imagined! It was so peaceful, I actually felt natural up there!" says Anne.

Josh agrees, but with a different sort of enthusiasm. "Woo-hoo! That was amazing! We flew sideways and did all sorts of dives and turns. It was absolutely awesome. Wow! I can't wait to do that again."
This concludes another short but thrilling adventure with Josh and Anne. Who knows where their next adventure may take us! Bye!

28.title: The Storm that Brought a Gift

paragraphs.text: There are two kinds of weather in Thailand: wet and dry. From April to October it rains every day. Almost six hundred years ago, there was a terrible storm in a city called Chiang Mai. It happened in 1434. Even though there was a strong wind, loud thunder, and deep puddles of rain, the people of Chiang Mai were not afraid. They were used to storms.

Outside the city was a small temple. There was a monk who lived at this temple and took care of the statues of Buddha. Whenever storms came, the monk would protect the incense so it didn't get wet. He wanted the incense to burn for Buddha.

After cleaning the temple, the monk stood in the doorway to watch the storm. The lightning stretched its fingers across the sky. The storm was coming closer to the temple. Just then, the monk saw a flash and heard a large crack! The lightning struck a chedi outside the temple and broke it.
A chedi is a bell-shaped pagoda. The first chedis contained the ashes of the Buddha and all chedis are sacred to his memory.
The monk ran out into the rain. He wanted to protect the memory of Buddha preserved in the broken chedi . The monk found an object on the ground, among the stone pieces from the broken chedi .

He wrapped the object in his robes and carried it into the temple. He lit a candle to see what it was. It looked like a statue of Buddha made out of rock. Because the statue was small, and it did not look valuable, the monk put the statue in his house. Every day he would clean this statue of Buddha and pray to it.

The monk took care of the statue for many years. But one day, when he was cleaning the statue, the nose fell off. "Oh no!" the monk cried. Then he looked again. There was another nose underneath, and it was green!
The monk carefully began to pull away the rock. Underneath was a second Buddha made of jade. The green was such a beautiful green that he named the statue The Emerald Buddha.
The monk sent a letter to the king, telling him the story of the Emerald Buddha. King Samfangkaen was excited. He asked for the statue to be sent to his palace in Chiang Mai.

The monk was sad to see the Emerald Buddha go. He put it on an elephant and sent it to Chiang Mai. But when the elephant got to the road, it would not go to Chiang Mai. This made the king angry, so he sent another elephant. This elephant would not go to Chiang Mai either. The king was very angry, so he sent a third elephant. This elephant did exactly what the first two had done.
The king thought, "Maybe the Emerald Buddha doesn't want to leave," so he stopped sending elephants. The jade statue of Buddha stayed with the monk for 32 more years.

Today the Emerald Buddha is kept in a temple called Wat Phra Kaew in Bangkok, Thailand. Three times a year there is a special ceremony when the king changes the clothes of the Emerald Buddha. The Emerald Buddha was a hidden treasure. What other hidden treasures are there waiting to be discovered?
Welcome to Mount Rushmore! My name is George Washington. I’m Thomas Jefferson. My name is Abraham Lincoln. And I’m Theodore Roosevelt. We are the presidents of Mount Rushmore.

Over fifty years ago, our faces were carved into these rocks here in the western state of South Dakota. You may be asking how the four of us got here. Well, that is a long story that began in December of 1923 with a man named Doane Robinson.

Doane Robinson was a true lover of American history. His dream was to capture western American history in the rocks of South Dakota in a way that had never been done before. He wanted to create a memorial that would make South Dakota famous.

You see, before our faces were put here, many people had never even heard of South Dakota, let alone come here for a vacation. But Robinson believed that people would love the mountains of South Dakota if there were something exciting to look at. Robinson talked to everyone he knew and told them about his great plan.

Of course, some people laughed at him and said that his plan was foolish, but many others listened to him. They agreed that carving the faces of famous Americans would be a great historical monument for the United States and would bring many tourists to their small state.

Within a few months, Robinson had convinced many important men, and they decided to start the project. Robinson found the only man in America that could do the job. His name was Gutzon Borglum. He was the most famous American artist and sculptor at that time.

When Gutzon heard about this project, he was very excited and boarded the first train for South Dakota. Robinson was thinking about carving the faces of Western heroes, such as General George Armstrong Custer, Buffalo Bill Cody, or Lewis and Clark. However, when Gutzon Borglum arrived, he told Robinson that he wished to carve the faces of more remarkable Americans that would illustrate the history of our country. Naturally, he was thinking about the four of us.

There are many mountains in South Dakota, but most of them were not suitable to carve our faces into. On some mountains, the rock was too soft or it had too many cracks in it. In other places, there was not enough sunlight, so our faces would always be in shadow. Gutzon searched for the perfect location.

Then one day Gutzon came to a tall cliff that was surrounded by pine trees. The name of the mountain was Mount Rushmore, near the little town of Keystone. The rock was flat and hard, and it had the perfect amount of sunlight. "Here is the place!" Gutzon cried. "I will carve America’s history here."

It took Gutzon Borglum and 400 men almost 14 years to carve our faces into these rocks. The workmen were miners who had spent their lives smashing rocks, so at first many of them considered it to be a normal job. Since they were poor, they were happy to earn money to buy food for their families. But as our faces began to appear, they became much more excited about their work. They were not simply making money; they knew they were building American history.

Norman Anderson was one of the carvers that helped make our faces look true to life. He was proud to say, "I put the curl in Lincoln’s beard, the part in Teddy’s hair, and the twinkle in Washington’s eye."

But how did these workmen make us look so lifelike? First, Gutzon made a statue of each of us, which he brought to the construction site. Then, using special measurement instruments, the workmen made an exact copy of the statues in the rock. The only difference was that the rock carving was 12 times bigger than the statues.

A protractor was placed at the top of the statues’ heads and a bigger one near the top of the mountain. To make Lincoln’s eye, for example, the workers would use a string attached to the protractor on the statue to measure the distance from the top of his head to the top of his eye. Then they would use a string attached to the protractor on the mountain that was 12 times longer.

Gutzon Borglum died just before our faces were completed, so he never got to see his final masterpiece. But his son, Lincoln Borglum, and the workmen spent one more year finishing this great piece of American history, which is now called Mount Rushmore.

In 1886 Gustave Eiffel, a very famous French builder, was chosen to build a tower in Paris for the 1889 International Exposition. However, when people first saw his drawings, they were not pleased. In fact, many people truly hated the new tower.
"What is this?" asked a famous artist.
"It is a picture of the new tower they are building for the International Exposition," replied his friend. "Do you like it?"
"No," declared the artist, "I hate it. It is the strangest-looking tower I have ever seen. It has no beauty and it will ruin Paris."

Around Paris, other people were saying the same thing. "The tower that Gustave Eiffel is building looks like a big streetlamp," wrote one newspaper reporter. "Eiffel is building a factory pipe," wrote another reporter.

Many of the artists and other important people wrote letters demanding that the Eiffel Tower not be built. They believed that Paris was too great a city for such a horrible tower. But thankfully, the people in charge did not listen to these complaints.

Gustave Eiffel was one of the first builders to use metal in his constructions. He was famous for building large and strong bridges and tall buildings made of metal. Before building the Eiffel Tower, he also designed and built the Statue of Liberty in New York City.

On July 1, 1887 Eiffel and his company began working on the tower. It was a very unusual building project because they first made all the pieces of the tower in a factory. Then they brought the pieces to Paris and put them together like a puzzle.

Each piece of the puzzle was put together with special nails called rivets. The rivets were so large that it took four men to put one in. Since there were over two million rivets, this was a very big job. But slowly the pieces were put together, and the tower went up and up and up.

By March 15, 1888, the workmen completed the first level. Then six months later, they had put the second level together. By March of 1889, the tower was completed and ready for the exposition. When it was finished, it was 324 meters tall and weighed more than 10,000 tons.
When the Eiffel Tower was finished, the people of Paris were very pleased with it. Those who thought that the tower would look ugly, now thought it was one of the most wonderful structures ever made.

Because the tower was made for visitors to the exposition, it needed to have elevators that could bring people up to the first, second, and top floors. Today that might seem easy, but in 1889 that was a very difficult job. No one had ever built elevators so high before.

In most buildings, the elevators go straight up and straight down, but not in the Eiffel Tower. Because of the shape of the tower, the elevators had to travel along a curve. When people first saw these unusual elevators, they were amazed and excited.

Because it was specifically built for the exposition, the Eiffel Tower was going to stay up for only a few years at first. But soon it became very popular and visitors from around the world came to see it. These days, over six million people visit the tower each year.

So instead of taking the tower down, Gustave Eiffel found other good uses for the tower. In the early 1900s, there was a new invention called the radio. In order to travel far distances, radio signals must come from radio towers that are very tall. So Gustave had the great idea of using the Eiffel Tower as a radio tower.

The Eiffel Tower is beautiful in the daytime because you can see the wonderful metal structure that Gustave built. However, it is also wondrous at night because there are more than 350 beautiful lights that cover it from head to toe. On top are two light beams that can be seen from over eighty kilometers away.

31.title: Christmas Hide and Seek 2: Reindeer Cheer

paragraphs.text: Billy followed one of the elves into Santa’s workshop. The elves were very busy packing up toys. Billy wanted to help, but the elves were too busy to tell him how. Billy decided to go look for his father. He saw his father talking to Santa Claus near the reindeer stables. Billy didn’t want to bother him, so he went into the stables instead.
Billy had never seen reindeer before, and he thought they were very big. Billy looked at the biggest one and said, "Wow, you’re much bigger than I thought you would be."
The reindeer nodded and said, "Yes, many people say that."
"Did you say something?" asked Billy. Animals aren’t supposed to talk!
"Yes, I did," said the reindeer matter-of-factly. "My name is Dasher. What’s your name?"
Billy understood. They were Santa’s reindeer, so of course they could talk. "My name is Billy. Santa said you were sick. Are you feeling better?" he asked.
"We’re not sick," said Dasher sadly. "We’re just really sad. We can’t fly if we’re sad."
"Oh, just like Peter Pan," said Billy. "When he taught Wendy and the boys to fly, he said they had to think happy thoughts."
Dasher nodded. "Yes, that’s right, but it’s hard to think happy thoughts when everyone is so busy. Santa doesn’t have time for us anymore. We’re lonely and we miss him."
Billy looked at Dasher and said, "If I bring Santa in here right now, will that make you happy?"
"Nothing can bring Santa in here on Christmas Eve. He’s too busy," said Dasher tearfully.
Billy didn’t want to see Dasher cry, so he said, "But if I bring Santa in here, would that make you happy?"
Dasher was sobbing quietly, so he didn’t answer, but Comet, Cupid, and Vixen said, "Yes, that would make us very happy."
Billy left the stable and ran to find his father and Santa Claus. He found them in Santa’s workshop, looking into a microscope.
"Well, it’s not an infection," said Doctor Vinton, stepping away from the microscope.
"I know what’s wrong with the reindeer, Daddy," said Billy. "They’re too sad to fly. It’s just like Peter Pan."
Billy’s father looked at Billy and said gently, "Billy, Peter Pan is a fairy tale. This is real, and the problem is real."
Santa stopped looking in the microscope and asked Billy, "Why are they sad?"
"They’re sad because you no longer have time to visit with them," said Billy. "They miss you and they want to see you."

Santa turned to Billy’s father and said, "Peter Pan is not a fairy tale. I knew Peter many years ago. He was such a wonderful boy, but like all boys, he grew up. I think Billy has solved our problem. If my reindeer are unhappy, they can’t fly. Only happy reindeer can fly."

Santa Claus left his workshop and went to the stables. Billy and his father waited. After a very long time, Santa returned. He was very happy. "Billy, you have saved Christmas. Thank you for making my reindeer happy. Ho, ho, ho!"
Billy watched the elves load Santa’s sleigh. Even though the elves kept putting more and more toys into the sleigh, the pile never got bigger.

When the elves finished loading the sleigh, Santa came with his reindeer. Dasher came up to Billy and said, "Thank you, Billy. Giving Santa back to us was a wonderful Christmas present. I hope Santa gives you something special."
"Oh, I’m sure he will," said Billy happily.
As Santa and his reindeer took off, Santa shouted down to Billy, his father, and the elves: "Merry Christmas to all, and to all a good night! Ho, ho, ho!"

32.title: Christmas Hide and Seek 1: Suitcase Surprise

paragraphs.text: It was Christmas Eve. Billy and his sister, Lindsey, were playing hide and seek. Billy was looking for a place to hide.
"Oh, no! I can’t go in there. Mom is busy making pies," said Billy.
"Oh, no! I can’t go in there either!" he said in a whisper.

Billy’s father was Doctor Vinton, a famous animal doctor. He was talking on the phone. He looked very worried. Billy knew he shouldn’t bother his father. "You say they’re sick? All of them? What’s wrong with them?" asked Billy’s father.
Billy ran upstairs. He ran into his parents’ bedroom. "She always checks under the bed," Billy said to himself.
"She always checks in the closets too," he whispered. "But she never looks in my father’s luggage. I’ll hide in there," said Billy happily.
". . . 98, 99, 100. Ready or not, here I come!" shouted Lindsey.
It was dark and warm in his father’s luggage. Billy soon fell asleep.
Downstairs, Billy’s father had just finished his telephone call with Santa Claus. Santa Claus had called to tell him that his reindeer were very sick—so sick that they couldn’t fly.
"They’re sending a car to take me to the airport. It should be here in a few minutes," said Doctor Vinton to his wife.
"What should I tell the kids?" asked his wife.
"Tell them that some animals are very sick, and I need to help them," he said.
There was a loud knock on the door. A man in a dark suit and dark glasses walked in. "Doctor Vinton, I’ve been sent by the president," said the gentleman. "Are you ready?" he asked.
"Yes," said Billy’s father. "I have a bag packed. It’s upstairs in the closet. Can you get it for me? I will get my instruments and some medicine from my office."
The man nodded and went upstairs. He found the bag in the closet. "Wow! This bag is heavy," said the man.

The man took the suitcase and put it in the car. Billy’s father joined the man in the car, and they drove to the airport. At the airport, the president’s plane was waiting to take Doctor Vinton to the North Pole.

When Billy woke up, he wasn’t sure where he was. He was very surprised. He saw his father speaking with Santa Claus. "Daddy! Daddy!" called Billy. "Where are we? And why are you talking to Santa Claus?"
Billy’s father was even more surprised than Billy. "What? How . . . how did you get here?" asked Billy’s father in amazement.
"I was playing hide-and-seek with Lindsey. I hid in your suitcase. She didn’t find me so I guess I won!" shouted Billy excitedly.

Santa Claus smiled and said, "Yes, Billy, you won, but your father and I are very busy. My reindeer are sick, and he needs to find out how to make them better. Will you be a good boy and help my elves?"
Welcome to my home. I live here in this little nest inside this large clock, which is here in this tall clock tower in the great city of London. I'm a Big Ben bird.

Big Ben is in the Palace of Westminster, which is the main government building in Britain. This is where the most important decisions in the United Kingdom are made. It is also where the prime minister works.

The clock tower is 97 meters tall, and it has a very unusual clock. Most clocks have only one face, but this clock has four faces. Each one looks in a different direction. That way, people from all around London can look up and see what time it is.

The clock does not need a battery or electricity like your clocks at home. This is an old-fashioned clock. It runs on weights. Increasing the weights slows the clock a tiny bit, while reducing the weights speeds it up a little. If the clock is not keeping perfect time, the clock master adds or removes one penny at a time until the weight is just right, and the clock keeps perfect time again. The clock master still uses the same old-fashioned pennies from when the clock was built.

I often hear people say, "Look over there. It's Big Ben." Most people think that Big Ben is the name of this tower. But did you know that Big Ben is not the name of the clock tower? It's the name of the biggest and most famous bell inside the tower. The tower itself is called St. Stephen's Tower.

Big Ben rings every hour of the day so that people can hear what time it is. A hammer strikes the great bell the same number of times as the hour. So if you count the number of times Big Ben rings, you'll know what time it is. There are other smaller bells in the tower as well. These play a short melody every 15 minutes to signal the quarter hours.

Big Ben is one of the biggest bells in the world. It is much taller than even a really tall man. Big Ben is 2.8 meters high, and it weighs 13,760 kilograms. That is more than the weight of 175 men. It was made on Saturday, April 10, 1858, and was named after Sir Benjamin Hall. Benjamin, or Ben for short, was a very large man who was in charge of buying the new bell for the St. Stephen's Tower clock.

One of the most amazing things about Big Ben is the place where it was made. Big Ben comes from the Whitechapel Bell Foundry here in London. The Whitechapel Bell Foundry is famous because many of the great bells in the world were made here.

But it is also famous because this factory is over four hundred years old. The Whitechapel Bell Foundry began in 1570 and is still in business today. It is the oldest company in Britain and one of the oldest companies in the world.
Since the opening of the Whitechapel Bell Foundry, there have been over 27 kings and queens in Britain. Some of them, like King George V and Queen Mary, even visited this factory.

The factory has always been on this same street. In 1670, during the Great Fire of London, the Whitechapel Bell Foundry burned down. But right after the fire, the owners rebuilt their factory just across the street. And that is where it still stands today.

The most famous bells that were made at the Whitechapel Bell Foundry are the Liberty Bell in the United States, the Great Bell of Montreal Cathedral in Canada, and of course, Big Ben. But now there are some new, very special bells that are being made at the factory.

They are called the Bells of September. Three large bells are being made to remember the very sad day when the World Trade Center in New York City was destroyed. The first one has just been finished. It was made to look exactly like the Liberty Bell.
Listen! Can you hear that? It's Big Ben ringing, so it must be twelve o'clock. I should hurry back to the bell tower now and get my lunch.

Hello, I'm Maria Rigatoni. Welcome to Italy, and welcome to my house. In Italy there is so much to see and so much to do. But best of all, there is so much to eat. Italy is famous for pizza, pasta, and the world's best ice cream.
Today I will be making spaghetti with tomato sauce for lunch.
The first thing we need to do is to make a nice pile of flour. Then we make a big hole in the top of our pile. Just like this. It's for the eggs.
Now carefully we crack four eggs into the hole. Add just a little bit of water, not too much. Next we mix all the ingredients together.
Now you have to knead the dough. This is the hard part. You have to push and fold, push and fold, push and fold. Keep kneading! It makes your hands sore.
Now the dough is perfect, but it has to sit for thirty minutes. While we wait, I'll tell you a story.
In the thirteenth century, there was an Italian man named Marco Polo. He was a great explorer and a famous Italian.

When Marco was only 14 years old, his father decided to go on a voyage of exploration. Marco begged his father to take him along, and finally his father agreed. They traveled all the way to China and they had great adventures.

During their voyage, Marco saw many things that Italians had never seen before, such as eyeglasses and ice cream. But best of all, he discovered long, thin noodles. Marco Polo brought these noodles to Italy, and we called them spaghetti.

Some historians claim that Marco Polo discovered noodles in the Arab world, and historians still debate whether he really discovered them in China. Nonetheless, it is widely accepted by the Italians that spaghetti noodles were first imported to Italy from China.

In the sixteenth century, the people who explored Mexico found fresh tomatoes. Because they were so delicious, they decided to bring some back to Europe. Soon we began to grow tomatoes in Italy.

Because of the warm sun and good soil, tomatoes grew very well in Italy. So we began making many kinds of foods from tomatoes. Tomato sauce is now the most famous Italian sauce. It is used for spaghetti and pizza.

The origin of April Fool's Day dates back so long ago that it is not clear when or how it got started. Some people say the day for fooling began in France when a king agreed to change the yearly calendar. He moved New Year's Day from April 1 to January 1. It was difficult to communicate in those days, so many people did not hear about the change. Some people continued to celebrate New Year's Day on April 1. These people were called April Fools.
When the king announced the new calendar, the neighbors in one village discussed it.
"Hey, did you hear that we have a new calendar?" said one.
"Yes, New Year's Day does not fall on April 1 anymore. Now, it is on January 1," said the other.
"Now we have to celebrate New Year's Day in January when it is cold."
"That's right. By the way, do you think Louis knows about this?"
"The whole village knows, but Louis will not accept it. As you know, he is a stubborn man."
Louis always insisted on being right. He did not listen very well to others, and his neighbors did not like him. "Louis always thinks that he is right."
"Yes, he does. Even when he is wrong, he never admits it," they said.
When Louis walked by, they called out, "Hey, Louis! Do you know we have to celebrate New Year's Day on January 1?"
"Ha-ha! You believe that rumor?" Louis laughed. "We always celebrate the New Year on April 1. You are so foolish!"
His neighbors decided this was a chance to play a trick on him. "Ha-ha! This is going to be fun!" they laughed.
The next day, Louis' neighbor called him into his house. "Hey Louis, will you do me a favor?"
"If I can," Louis said.
"Look, I broke my leg," said his neighbor, "so I cannot deliver this important message to the lord of the next village. Will you take it for me?"
"I have work to do," said Louis. "But it is not far to the next village, so I'll do it. But just this once!"
Louis went to the next village and knocked at the door of the lord. "Hi, this letter is from our village," he said when a servant answered.
The servant read the letter and laughed. "Interesting! But I am sorry. This letter is not for the lord of this village. Would you deliver this to the lord in the next village?"

So Louis went to the next village. The servant of the lord of that village also laughed when he read it. "Thank you, but this letter is not for my master. Please take it over to the lord of the next village."

Louis thought this was very strange. "Didn't my friend know the right village to send this letter to?" he wondered. "The next village is too far away. I think that I have walked far enough! My friend must be wrong! I will return the letter to him."

So Louis returned home. He was very tired. He sat at his table and thought, "Hmm, why did everyone laugh when they read this letter?" Out of curiosity, he opened it. The letter said: The new calendar moved New Year's Day from April 1 to January 1. But I will celebrate New Year's Day on April 1 because I refuse to change. I am an April Fool. Please send me to the lord of the next village.
